reason: E3 directly supports the existence of edge-dislocation-dominated plasticity in a BCC HEA, but none of the cited evidence links this phenomenon to grain refinement, the proposed mechanism, or the predicted strength optimum. E1 and E2 are about different materials or structures and do not support the key premises.
premises: Grain refinement can induce a transition from screw-dominated to edge dislocation-mediated plasticity in single-phase HEAs.
Edge dislocations are less temperature sensitive and more effective at impeding plastic flow than screw dislocations.
This transition enhances hardness and yield strength up to an optimal grain size, beyond which softening occurs.
The optimal grain size for this transition is in the tens of nanometers range for BCC HEAs.
The mechanism is driven by increased grain boundary density promoting edge dislocation nucleation and mobility.
